DATED 30.05.2022 IN W.P.NO.2542/2022 (LA-RES) PASSED BY THIS HON'BLE COURT PRODUCED HEREWITH AS ANNEXURE-A AND PUNISH THE ACCUSED IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.

THIS CCC, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE K.SOMASHEKAR  AND  HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S RACHAIAH  -4-  NC: 2024:KHC:32914-DB  CCC No. 822 of 2022
ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE K.SOMASHEKAR)

The present Contempt proceeding is initiated by the complainants against the respondent / Authority, seeking to initiate contempt of Court proceedings against the respondent / accused for willful disobedience of the order dated 30.05.2022 in W.P.No.2542/2022 passed by this Court vide Annexure-"A".
2.
Learned counsel Shri Pavana Chandra Shetty H for complainants is present.
Further, learned AGA for Accused is also present.

Puttalingaiah vs Mr Manjunath, K.A.S on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186175258/
3 3.

Learned AGA prays for consideration of the affidavit dated 19.12.2023, sworn to by Shri Binoy P.K, S/o. P.V. Vijayan, presently serving as the Assistant Commissioner, Ramanagara Sub-Division,
Ramanagara.
4.

It is stated in the affidavit that Mr. Manjunath was impleaded as Accused No.1 in the present Contempt Petition in his official capacity as Assistant Commissioner, NC: 2024:KHC:32914-DB Ramanagara Sub-Division.

However, Mr. Manjunath has now been transferred from the said office as on 02.08.2023 and thereafter, the present Officer Shri Bijoy P.K. who has filed this affidavit has taken charge of the said post and that he is aware of the facts and circumstances of the present case.
5. It is further stated that the present Contempt Petition has been filed, citing willful disobedience of the order dated 30.05.2022 passed by this Court, in W.P.No.2542/2022.

By the said order, a learned Single Judge of this Court had issued a mandamus to consider the representation of the petitioners dated 07.01.2022 and pass necessary orders within two months, taking into consideration the losses that have been caused to the payment of compensation.
Further, the respondents were directed to act on the said representation without reference to any delay.
Report was to be filed by the Additional Chief Secretary within a period of three months.

In compliance of the order dated 30.05.2022, it is stated in the affidavit that the representations of complainants have already been individually considered by the office of the Assistant Commissioner, Ramanagara Sub-Division, in order to evaluate their eligibility for enhanced compensation in terms of the applicable law.
Upon such consideration, detailed orders have been passed in respect of the claim of each of the complainants, as on 12.08.2022.
Thus, it is submitted that the claim of each of the complainants for enhancement of compensation has been rejected.

The said copies have been marked as Annexure-"R1".
7.

In view of the same, it is submitted in the affidavit that the directions of this Court have been duly complied with, though there has been some delay in such compliance, due to administrative constraints.
Hence, the learned AGA prays to consider the said affidavit and to thereby to drop the present Contempt proceedings.

Whereas, learned counsel for complainants has taken us through the representation dated 07.01.2022 Annexure-"D" filed by the complainants, which is addressed to the i) Deputy Commissioner, Ramanagara District, ii) Assistant Commissioner, Land Acquisition and iii) Commissioner, Ramanagara-Channapattana Authority.
In the said representation, the complainants have sought for grant of higher compensation as per the Land Acquisition Act.
It is stated in the representation that by fixing Rs.1,20,000/- per acre as compensation, the complainants are unable to purchase even 5 guntas of land from the said award.
It is stated that the rate per acre of land in Ramanagara District as on today is more than Rs.2,75,00,000/-.

The award Puttalingaiah vs Mr Manjunath, K.A.S on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186175258/
4 has been passed by the Authority as on 12.01.2016 fixing the compensation at Rs.1,20,000/- per acre, which exercise has been done after a period of more than 20 years.
However, even after the award, the compensation amount not having been paid by the Authority, the complainants had approached this Court by way of a writ petition in W.P.No.2758/2020.

Hence, a learned Single Judge of this Court by its order dated 01.02.2021 had directed the Assistant Commissioner of Land Acquisition to disburse the amount within 10 weeks from the date of release of the order, along with interest for the delayed payment in terms of Section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Thereafter, the complainants had filed another writ petition in W.P.No.2542/2022, wherein a learned Single Judge of this Court by order dated 30.05.2022,
issued a writ of mandamus directing the Assistant Commissioner of Land Acquisition, Ramanagara Sub-Division to consider the representation of the complainants dated 07.01.2022 and to pass necessary orders.
It is thereafter by order dated 12.08.2022 that the concerned Assistant Commissioner has passed an order rejecting the representation of the complainants.

9. In view of the fact that the representation of the complainants has already been rejected by the concerned Authority, learned counsel for the complainants prays for a NC: 2024:KHC:32914-DB direction to this Court to reserve liberty to the complainants to approach the appropriate Forum, to redress their grievance.
10. In view of the above, the compliance affidavit filed by the Assistant Commissioner is hereby taken on record and accepted.
Hence, the Contempt Petition is hereby disposed of.

11. However, keeping in view the submission of the learned counsel for the complainants in the presence of the learned counsel for the respondent / State, liberty is reserved to the complainants to approach the appropriate Forum, in accordance with law.
